context_heading: One key thing to understand about CIS and accountants
context: In the UK, the word 'accountant' on its own is not a protected title, so anyone can call themselves an accountant. However, titles such as Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant are protected, and members are bound by their professional body's ethics, training and complaints rules. It's reasonable to ask which professional body, if any, an accountant belongs to.

Every accountancy practice offering services must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC. You can ask which body supervises the firm, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and how complaints are handled. This helps you make an informed choice.

faqs.q: What is the Construction Industry Scheme (CIS)?
faqs.a: The Construction Industry Scheme is a UK tax scheme for contractors and subcontractors in the construction industry. Contractors deduct tax from subcontractors' payments and pass it to HMRC, and subcontractors can reclaim overpaid tax.

faqs.q: Do I need a CIS accountant if I'm a subcontractor?
faqs.a: If you're a subcontractor, you may be able to reclaim tax deducted under CIS, especially if you operate through a limited company. An accountant can help you claim back what you're owed and keep your records straight.

faqs.q: What happens if I file my CIS returns late?
faqs.a: Late CIS returns can attract penalties from HMRC. An accountant can help you get up to date and avoid further penalties.

faqs.q: Can I reclaim CIS deductions if I'm a limited company?
faqs.a: Yes, limited company subcontractors can offset CIS deductions against their tax bill. An accountant can guide you through the process.

extra_heading: Finding a CIS accountant close to your site work
extra: Searching for a CIS accountant near me often comes from someone who moves between sites and wants an accountant they can actually reach, whether that means dropping paperwork in or having a face-to-face conversation about deductions. Construction work rarely fits neatly into office hours, so it is worth asking early how a practice prefers to communicate and whether they can work around your schedule.

When you compare local accountants, ask specifically how they handle CIS rather than accountancy in general. A practice that deals with the scheme regularly will know the difference between a contractor's monthly return and a subcontractor's claim to offset deductions, and will be comfortable reading payment and deduction statements. Ask what they need from you and how they keep track of deadlines so late returns do not creep up.

It also helps to be clear about your own setup before you call. Whether you are a sole trader, a partnership or a limited company changes what can be reclaimed and how records should be kept, and a local accountant will want to know this at the first conversation. Being upfront about any returns already overdue means they can tell you honestly what they can take on.

At a first appointment, expect to talk through your CIS status, the statements you have received and how your business is structured, so the accountant can explain what they would do and quote you for it. It is a conversation, not a commitment, and it is a good moment to ask which body supervises the firm and whether they hold professional indemnity insurance.

extra_faqs.q: Does my accountant need to be local to my building site?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily, but many people searching for a CIS accountant near me want someone they can visit or call easily when paperwork builds up. It is worth asking how a practice handles documents and queries before you decide whether distance matters for you.

extra_faqs.q: Can a CIS accountant help if I am both a contractor and a subcontractor?
extra_faqs.a: Some people in construction work both ways, taking on subcontractors for some jobs and being paid as a subcontractor on others. Explain this when you enquire so the accountant can tell you how they would handle both sides of the scheme for you.

extra_faqs.q: What should I bring to a first meeting about CIS?
extra_faqs.a: Bring your payment and deduction statements, details of your business structure and any correspondence from HMRC, including penalty notices. Having these to hand lets the accountant give you a clearer picture of what help you need and what they would charge.
